A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same StarDojo benchmark. Their main text, tables, figures, algorithm, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven models on StarDojo-Lite in Table 3 and observation-modality and real-time ablations in Figure 4.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds quantified GPT-4.1 failure analysis and illustrated agent trajectories in Section 4.2 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: The StarDojoMod/Python architecture, observation and action interfaces, pause/resume mechanism, task initialization, evaluation Algorithm 1, and prompted agent procedure are retained. Expanded or shortened explanations do not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Evaluation retains StarDojo-Lite and the same five-task ablation coverage. All 100 task entries and their configurations in Table 5 match. The new case studies concern existing tasks rather than new domains or test conditions.

E2.justification: Table 3 retains GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1 mini, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Llama 4 Maverick, Qwen2.5 VL 72B, and Gemma 3 27B. Ablation comparators also remain unchanged. AvalonBench is added to the descriptive related-work comparison, not experimentally evaluated.

E3.justification: The added error analysis specifies reporting the primary error blocking progress when a task contains multiple errors (v3 Section 4.2). Existing benchmark settings retain 720p images, 7×7 textual surroundings, two-action outputs, and 30/50/150-step budgets; relocating these disclosures does not change those settings.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's qualitative discussion and retained ablations, v3 adds quantitative failure categorization, four illustrated error cases, and paired successful/failed trajectories for tilling, fertilizing, and purchasing beer (Section 4.2; Appendix E, Figures 7–8). This substantially expands the diagnostic evidence.

E5.justification: Both versions report three runs and success-rate means with standard deviations in Table 3; the ablation captions also retain three runs. The added error frequencies introduce no new uncertainty estimates, significance tests, or repeated-run reporting procedure.

E6.justification: All 168 mean/standard-deviation pairs in Table 3 and the ablation plots are unchanged, including GPT-4.1's 12.7±0.6% overall success. New diagnostic results attribute errors to visual understanding (42%), multimodal reasoning (21%), long-term planning (21%), and low-level control (16%), with additional subtype frequencies and trajectory findings.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. The task-completion rule and Algorithm 1 are unchanged; the expanded production–social coupling discussion is conceptual explanation rather than new mathematical theory.

C1.justification: v3 adds the explicit priority claim that StarDojo is the first benchmark combining production and living (Section 5), whereas v1 describes it as novel. The principal benchmark contribution, 1,000-task/100-task scope, and headline performance claim remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 elaborates production–social feedback, discusses inconsistent planning and insufficient game knowledge, and adds an inference-efficiency versus capability tradeoff. Section 5 newly limits the social-intelligence interpretation to socially situated embodied decision-making rather than comprehensive open-ended social intelligence.

D1.justification: Table 6 corrects the swapped model identifiers for Gemini 2.5 Pro and GPT-4.1 mini, aligning them with the models already specified in the experiments. The task configurations, simulator APIs, evaluation pseudocode, prompt, and installation/access information otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 removes the Avalon RL-generalization reference and adds WOLF and AvalonBench; AvalonBench also enters Table 1. The introduction more explicitly contrasts social-deduction environments with coupled production/social constraints, while retaining the broader related-work framework.

P1.justification: Existing introduction and gameplay-description paragraphs are substantially rewritten, task difficulty receives an expanded main-text explanation, and the qualitative discussion is reorganized around tool use, navigation, and long-horizon tasks. Separate error-analysis and case-study sections and revised appendix organization further change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The document adopts a different page format, typography, running headers, and extensive figure/table reflow. v3 adds the error-distribution chart and two case-study figures. Table 1 gains AvalonBench and revised column headings; the unchanged ablation figure is renumbered from Figure 4 to Figure 5.

improvement.justification: The quantified failure analysis and concrete trajectories strengthen support for previously mostly qualitative diagnoses, while the social-scope clarification and corrected model identifiers improve precision. These are useful but limited gains: the core evaluation is unchanged, error-labeling details remain sparse, and some rewritten passages introduce repetition or awkward wording.
